sweep Aug23: Porto are now the concrete suitor. sweep Aug23: There is still no 2026 US measles death; ProPublica (Aug 18) counts 3 deaths since the start of 2025, all in 2025. Pennsylvania cases are 'surging' (Lehigh Valley Aug 4, Pittsburgh Aug 10/21), Texas has school-season cases, Florida has an outbreak (Donalds on CBS, Aug 23), and Utah is slowing.

sweep Aug23: The Kalshi market (Aug 16) has Bruno Fernandes at 83c and Rice at 19c, with others at 1-2c. The ceremony is Aug 25. Bruno already won the FWA award and PL Player of the Season, while Arsenal's three nominees may split the vote.

sweep Aug23: TASS (Aug 23) reports the Witkoff/Kushner Moscow visit is delayed and 'unlikely before the end of August'. The Kremlin (Aug 19-20) had no date, and Zakharova says Moscow could arrange a meeting at short notice. No US official has visited Moscow in August so far; Gilman was released Aug 11 with no official in Moscow. Conditional on a CBS-reported visit, Witkoff is still the likeliest.

sweep Aug23: FootballTransfers/Athletic (Aug 18) say Chelsea keeping Emegha all but confirms Jackson leaves permanently (asking EUR65-75m). Schira (Aug 13) says talks with Villa are progressing and Jackson has said yes, and Villa had no fit centre-forward at Brighton on Aug 23 with Watkins heading to Al Hilal. No club-to-club fee has been agreed yet.

sweep Aug23: Liverpool made an improved EUR135m bid (Aug 17) and PSG are reportedly willing to take EUR130-140m. RMC (Aug 17) says an agreement is expected and Romano says Barcola has agreed personal terms. Barcola was left out of PSG squads on Aug 16 and Aug 22 pending a move. Arsenal have had no club-to-club talks, so conditional on a move it is overwhelmingly Liverpool.

sweep Aug23: Juventus are out after signing Vicario on loan (Aug 17), and Villa signed Suzuki (Aug 19). Emery confirmed Martinez asked to leave (Aug 21), and he was absent from Villa's squad on Aug 23 with the Guardian calling him 'set to leave'. Tottenham need a keeper after Vicario's exit and are the bookmakers' favourites (talkSPORT 2/1, Aug 19), ahead of a Saudi club (6/1), Chelsea (10/1) and Man Utd (16/1).

sweep Aug23: Manchester City (Maresca) are now the only real suitor. They missed Chelsea's Aug 14 deadline for the GBP120m price, but reports (Aug 21-23) say they are still interested and may bid late, and Enzo told Chelsea he wants to leave. Real Madrid now have Mourinho and Bernardo Silva and have not been linked lately.

sweep Aug23: BBC and GiveMeSport (Aug 23) report Al-Hilal in talks with Arsenal, willing to top Galatasaray's EUR45m bid, and Martinelli is open to the move. Arsenal want EUR60-70m and Arteta has told him he is surplus. He rejected Galatasaray (Aug 13-14), and no other top-five-league club has made concrete interest.

sweep Aug23: Everton and Ipswich contacted Arsenal (AS via Mirror/TransferFeed, Aug 19-20), and Jesus wants to stay in the PL. Moretto (Aug 20) says he is 'not currently open' to Napoli despite a claimed GBP17m club deal (low-quality source, Aug 15). Milan look unlikely after their club-record Goncalo Ramos signing. Arsenal want GBP17-20m.

sweep Aug23: Ynet (Aug 22): Ra'am's national conference chose its slate as 1 Abbas, 2 Walid Taha, 3 Walid al-Huashla, 4 Iman Khatib-Yasin, 5 Yasser Hajirat, with slots 6+ and links to independents left to the executive committee. Segalovitz wanted No. 2 (Haaretz, Jul 31) and talks were ongoing on Aug 13, so a reshuffle is the main risk.

sweep Aug23: Rogers (GBP117m to Chelsea) still leads Anderson (GBP116m) and Tonali (about GBP98m). Liverpool's EUR135m bid for Barcola is about GBP116m, and PSG want EUR140-150m, so a completed deal could top Rogers. Chelsea value Enzo at GBP120m with City interested. Arsenal may bid for Alvarez if Atletico relent (GMS, Aug 23).

sweep Aug23: Renard took the Ivory Coast job in early August, so he is out. Talks with Queiroz collapsed over a USD150k/month demand (Pulse, Aug 14), but the GFA ExCo unanimously recommended keeping him, pending Sports Ministry approval and funding (Aug 18-20). Assistant Desmond Ofei is 'widely expected' to take interim charge for the Sep 23 qualifier against Ivory Coast, and Beaumelle has applied.

sweep Aug23: Trump and Bessent promise the 'most crushing' economic war on Iran, with details due at an Aug 24 press conference. Treasury has warned two unnamed larger Chinese banks and in recent weeks targeted Dubai exchange houses and shell firms (Aug 7). Chinese banks are the most-discussed target but carry Xi-visit risk; no bank has been named.

sweep Aug23: International sugar prices rose about 19% in August to Aug 19, with NY raws at a 14-month high (17.48c) and London whites at a 16-month high, and India is importing 1Mt of raw sugar (Aug 21). By comparison, wheat is up about 6.5% this month on the Black Sea halt (Aug 20), and crude rose about 6% (veg oils) while palm supply is comfortable. July FFPI: sugar +5.6%, cereals +3.4%, veg oils +2%.

sweep Aug23: Kalimantan fires are intensifying; Prabowo visited on Aug 22, sent three battalions and helicopters, and more than 200k ha burned Jan-Jul, worse than 2019 or 2023. Haze reached Sarawak, where the API hit 227 ('very unhealthy') in Serian on Aug 21, and Malaysia asked ASEAN to act (Aug 22), with El Nino strengthening. Malaysia is raised toward its API>500 emergency threshold.

sweep Aug23: In Madrid's opener at Espanyol (2-1, Aug 22), Bellingham headed the 9th-minute opener as an attacking midfielder, and Mbappe was not at his sharpest. Betis signed Troy Parrott (EUR20m, Aug 19-21), who may start ahead of Cucho.

sweep Aug23: Salon (Aug 22): Talarico has spent $25M+ on ads against Paxton's $119k and leads narrowly, Cook moved Texas to toss-up, and Republicans expect the 'cavalry' (SLF/MAGA Inc) soon. MAGA Inc's roughly $400M is still unspent, and Leavitt joins it at the end of August. The GOP plans to 'spend heavily' in Michigan against El-Sayed (WSJ, Aug 23).

sweep Aug23: Antonelli will take a grid penalty of at least 10 places, possibly starting at the back, at Monza for a full power-unit change (Wolff, Aug 23). Norris won the Dutch GP from pole (Aug 23), his second straight win with McLaren upgrades. Russell won the Dutch sprint and is Mercedes' lead at Monza. Hamilton was 4th and Leclerc 5th.

sweep Aug23: Bloomberg/ST (Aug 20): transmission is accelerating outside Ituri, with confirmed cases growing about twice as fast in North Kivu and Haut-Uele over the past week and Tshopo jumping more from a small base. Haut-Uele treatment centres are over capacity (Wamba at 4x beds) and Bas-Uele is a new area. Totals are 5,208 cases and 2,476 deaths, and the UN calls the growth 'exponential' (Aug 21).

sweep Aug23: In matchday one Barcelona won 5-0 at Elche (Aug 23) and Real Madrid won 2-1 at Espanyol with a 90th-minute goal in Mourinho's return (Aug 22). The big two remain near co-favourites, with Barca slightly ahead on form and goal difference.

sweep Aug23: 1892 Holdings (Bezos's K5 fund, Saverin, Mittal trusts) bought about 38% of Liverpool on Aug 14, with an option to take control, which makes Amazon a plausible new front-of-shirt partner. There is no sponsor news, and Standard Chartered reportedly won't renew after 2026-27.

sweep Aug23: England won the 1st Test by an innings with an all-seam attack (Aug 21). Robinson and Tongue took all 10 first-innings wickets (both 5-fers) and 8 each in the match; Archer took 3 and Atkinson 1 in the second innings. Carse was arrested in Derby on Aug 22 and is under ECB investigation, so he is dropped. Robinson is added.

Kyiv Independent (Aug 1) says the gas-station campaign is spreading from the east and south into central Ukraine (Pyriatyn hit Jul 3). Russia destroyed every station in Poltava Oblast's Opishnya hromada on Aug 9, and NV (Aug 5) lists hits in Chernihiv, Sumy, Kyiv, Odesa, Poltava and even Ternopil oblasts. Recent repeat hits are still mostly in near-front Kharkiv, Zaporizhzhia and Kryvyi Rih, so Poltava now leads the far-from-front cities.

On Aug 12-13 Houthi armed boats carrying drones attacked Zuqar and Mayun islands and were repelled by Yemeni army and coast guard forces stationed there (Okaz, PTOC). On Aug 19 Yemen's information minister told AFP that the Houthis plan to seize the Bab al-Mandab coast, Mokha, the Hanish islands and Mayun, so Houthi risk was raised. Government-aligned forces still hold the island, and the label AP or Al Jazeera will use is uncertain.

Sinner withdrew with a knee injury (Aug 21). Shelton won Montreal (Aug 13, beating Nakashima in the final) but lost in Cincinnati R1. Fritz won Washington. Tiafoe reached the Cincinnati final (lost to Fils, Aug 23), and Nakashima made the Montreal final and Cincinnati SF, beating Fritz. Projected seeds are Shelton 8, Fritz 9, Tien 12, Nakashima ~18, Tiafoe ~19 and Paul ~20; the draw is about Aug 27.

Ingebrigtsen is back from Achilles surgery: he won the European 5000m on Aug 10 (13:15.29) in his first race in 324 days and is auto-qualified for the UC 5000m (Sep 11 straight final) as Olympic champion. He was only 4th in the Silesia 1500m on Aug 23, behind Strand, Koech and Hocker. Yihune holds the 12:47 world lead, and Hocker is the 2025 world champion.

AFP/Le Parisien (Jul 11): the trial is Sep 10-11 with three adults. Kherbouch 'Ganito' is the alleged co-mastermind, a recidivist with a prior 7-year sentence, and was recaptured 13 days after his March escape. Khyan M. is the co-mastermind and the third is an executant who was himself sequestered by them. Kherbouch's record makes him the likeliest to get the longest sentence.

Yan remains the class of the field (71.74 WR-U20 ratified Jul 23; unbeaten in four DL meetings through Monaco). There is no news on whether she will contest Budapest (Sep 12) before the Asian Games, and the UC's 8-6-4 reduction format adds variance. Kitaguchi is auto-qualified as Olympic champion, and Kolak won the Euro title with only 62.43.

The official competition lineup (Jul 23; jury president Maggie Gyllenhaal) has 21 films; Amelio's Nessun dolore and Out of This World are not in it. The Special Jury Prize skews to political or Eastern European auteur films (No Bears, Green Border, Dear Comrades!) and Italian titles (2019, 2021, 2025). That favours Khrzhanovsky's DAU, Ali Asgari's A Bit of Light and Moretti's It Will Happen Tonight.

Talks have been frozen since the Iran war began. The Witkoff/Kushner trip to Kyiv and Moscow, promised Jul 29, has been postponed past end-August (TASS, Aug 23), and Peskov saw no grounds for optimism (Aug 20). Earlier rounds were held in Abu Dhabi and Geneva, and the US floated Miami in February, so the United States stays the top pick with Switzerland and Turkey next.

Norris has won two in a row (Hungary in late July; Dutch GP from pole on Aug 23). Antonelli was 2nd, extending his lead to 59 over Russell and Hamilton, and Russell won the Dutch sprint. Antonelli takes a 10+ place grid drop at Monza, not Madrid. Mercedes remain the best car, but McLaren are now on par and Ferrari were close (Hamilton P4, Leclerc P5).

Tebogo won the Lausanne 200m in a dominant 19.87 on Aug 21 (SB 19.84). Lyles won the US 100m in a world-leading 9.79 but pulled up with cramp in the US 200m final (Jul 26). Both are confirmed 'Ultimate Stars' for the Sep 13 200m (Aug 18). Tate Taylor beat Tebogo in Eugene.

Pathirage keeps winning: Commonwealth gold (89.75) and Lausanne DL on Aug 21 (88.14), ahead of Chopra (88.05) and Peters (86.69), his third win over Chopra this year. Weber won the European title with a championship record (Aug 16). Nadeem is auto-qualified but out of form.

Gold Derby (Aug 17) has Seehorn at 79.7% to Russell's 14.7%. Ladbrokes (Aug 19) prices Seehorn at 1/5 and Russell at 15/4, and Kalshi had Seehorn at 77-81%. Seehorn won the Globe and Critics Choice, while Russell won the Actor Award.

SPACECOM's Gen. Whiting (Aug 12, Huntsville) said the US needs 'credible, acknowledged' kinetic and non-kinetic space fires. Today only the ground-based CCS/Meadowlands is acknowledged, and the Golden Dome interceptor demos are slated for 2027 (Aug 8). The Sep 14 resolution date may coincide with the AFA conference, the usual venue for Space Force disclosures, so the US is raised. A null outcome in 2026 is still quite possible.

Hacks leads but Widow's Bay is close: Gold Derby (Aug 17) has 74/25, Ladbrokes (Aug 19) 3/4 vs evens, and Kalshi (Jul 17) 55/43 with the gap narrowing. Matthew Rhys is a 90% favourite for Widow's Bay in Comedy Actor, and Jean Smart is a near-lock for Hacks.

The Pitt is an overwhelming favourite to repeat: Gold Derby (Aug 17) has it at 91.6%, Ladbrokes at 1/10, prediction markets around 90%, and every Ankler pundit picks it (Aug 19). Pluribus is a distant second at 6-12%, and AKOTSK is 10/1 at Ladbrokes.

London's final bid (Aug 6) now has a venue agreement with London Stadium/West Ham plus government funding. Nairobi submitted (Aug 10) with Ruto's personal guarantee for Kasarani. Coe said the 2029 and 2031 hosts will be named together on Sep 15 from London, Rome, Munich and Nairobi, and India/Ahmedabad is no longer listed. London is ready-made for 2029, with Nairobi possibly getting 2031.

Pakistan already urged Tehran to restrain the Houthis over threats to Saudi shipping (The Nation, Jul 23), and signed a Saudi-Turkey-Pakistan mutual defence pact in Mecca (Aug 7). China is the guarantor of the Saudi-Iran Beijing deal and has precedent (Reuters 2024). Saudi Arabia talks to the Houthis via Omani mediators, and Japan publicly said it asked Iran to urge restraint (Aug 19). No Reuters report has appeared yet.

Cruz Azul beat Toluca 3-1 in the Campeón de Campeones (Jul 25; Paradela scored twice), so they face MLS Cup holders Inter Miami in Miami on Sep 16 and Toluca is out. Miami have home advantage and Messi (scoring again in August) but were eliminated in the Leagues Cup group stage. Liga MX sides won the last three Campeones Cups.

Republicans have been silent on Trump-family self-dealing, such as Don Jr.'s Kazakhstan tungsten venture, defence-firm stakes and UAE money in World Liberty (MS NOW, Aug 20). A request would most likely come from a lame duck: retiring Judiciary member Tillis, Cassidy after his primary loss, or Cornyn, a Judiciary member who lost his primary runoff to Paxton. Cornyn replaces McConnell in the list.

Nike's deal lapsed Jul 31, but Nike launched a new Mbappe signature Mercurial on Aug 10, which he promoted. L'Equipe reports Nike has a 6-month right to match any offer, and Sportune (Aug 22) says Adidas withdrew months ago over his demands, with Puma and Under Armour weak. Reports (Aug 9-14) of an 'unexpected' new brand with an equity stake persist (Li-Ning denied), but with no announcement the question defaults to incumbent Nike.

Van vs Pantoja 2 is official as the UFC 331 main event (Aug 6). Odds are a pick'em: Pantoja opened -120/-105 and Van now -103 to -120 across books (BFO, Aug). Van is on a 7-fight streak including a defence over Taira, while Pantoja (36) returns from the elbow dislocation. Small mass is kept on replacements.

The co-main is Tsarukyan vs Mauricio Ruffy, not Oliveira, who withdrew after teammate Nascimento's death (Aug 6). Tsarukyan is a -350 to -400 favourite against Ruffy at +280 to +315; Ruffy has 13 KOs and stopped Chandler in June. The pick is shaded toward Ruffy for KO upside and Tsarukyan's withdrawal history.

Kenya's half marathon team (named Aug 21) is Ngetich, the world XC champion with a 1:03:04 PB who is 'the fastest woman in the field' and has won 5 of 6 races this year, plus Kasait, Jerono and Loleo. Chemnung, Jepchirchir and Chepkirui are not selected. Ethiopia's team is not yet known, so a large share is left unassigned.

The draw (Aug 7) is Group A Japan/Korea/Saudi/Indonesia, B Iran/Jordan/Chinese Taipei/Qatar, and C China/Philippines/Bahrain/Kazakhstan. QFs are Sep 16, SFs Sep 18, and the bronze game Sep 20. Bronze tends to go to a strong SF loser, so the six contenders (with Jordan about 0.11) are close.

No spring-1405 national accounts are out yet; last year's spring report came on Sep 22. In spring 1404 the largest subsector fall was water and electricity (-11.8%) and agriculture (-2.7%) was the worst group, while oil grew 0.8%. The April-June 2026 US naval blockade of Iranian ports should make oil the biggest decliner, but group-level reporting (oil inside 'industries and mines') remains a risk.

Forsa (Aug 4-18, pub Aug 22): Linke 22, CDU 18, AfD 18, Greens 16, SPD 12. Insa (Aug 7-13): CDU 20, Linke 19, AfD 17, Greens 16, SPD 15, and recent polls have rotated CDU/Linke/AfD on top. Wegner resigned and the CDU now runs Stefan Evers; Linke also topped Berlin in the 2025 federal vote.

Real Madrid won 2-1 at Espanyol with a 90th-minute goal on Aug 22 in Mourinho's first game. Atletico beat Malaga 2-0, then drew 2-2 at Villarreal on Aug 23 while fans jeered Alvarez, who wants to leave. The derby is at the Metropolitano and is close to a coin flip.

Yu Yiting set a Chinese record of 2:06.82 at the June nationals, where Yu Zidi was 2nd. She then beat McIntosh to win the Pan Pacs 200 IM in 2:07.45 (Aug 15). Yu Zidi (PB 2:07.41) remains the main threat.

No reports of CPS charges up to Aug 23 (archive and searches). The five long-standing suspects and the unnamed man arrested in Gateshead in 2024 are all still uncharged, so mass is left unassigned for the Gateshead suspect.

Yu Zidi won the 400 IM at the June 19 Chinese nationals in 4:30.79 (8th-fastest performer ever), ahead of Ke Wenxi (4:33.59). Yu Yiting has a 4:33.09 season best, and Narita tied for world silver in 2025 (4:33.26).

Ri Song Gum is the 2023 Asiad champion, set world records in 2025 and is on the DPRK delegation list. Mirabai won CWG 48kg gold and will lift in 49kg at the Asiad (HT, Aug 4). China's entrant is unconfirmed.

Ohashi led most of the Pan Pacs 200 breast final (Aug 15) but faded to bronze in 2:08.27, well off his 2:06.59. China's Asiad roster has Qin Haiyang and Dong Zhihao, and Watanabe is also on Japan's team.

The opener is Portugal v Wales on Sep 24 at Alvalade, reported (Jul 25) as Ronaldo's possible farewell. Ronaldo (scoring for Al Nassr Aug 22) calls 2026-27 'probably my last year' but has not quit Portugal. Draw risk is about 22%.

Japan's 100m entrants are Shuhei Tada (national champion) and Yuki Koike (10.06, 2026 best); Kiryu is relay-only (JAAF Jun 15). Puripol stays the favourite, and Korea's Nwamadi has run 10.13 (10.07 wind-aided, Aug).

The 6th Cir. panel (Ohio/Tennessee, argued Jul 30) appeared ready to side with the states, and the 4th Cir. Maryland panel (argued May 7) was openly skeptical of Kalshi. The 9th Cir. Nevada appeal is pending, the 2nd Cir. sent Kalshi's CT/NY injunction motions to a panel (Aug 19), and Utah's win (Aug 4) is on appeal to the 10th Cir.

TikTok keeps settling private bellwether cases before trial (three more on Aug 3), but no state settlement yet. Utah's trial is not until June 2027 (Jul 29 order), Pennsylvania sued on Aug 11 and Florida on Jun 15.
Rohit told Vimal Kumar (reported Aug 13) that the 2027 WC is his 'last chance' and he cannot play another. That makes him the likeliest to repeat it inside the Sep 1-20 window.

Hamburg withdrew after its referendum failed (54.9% no). The DOSB assembly picks between Berlin, Munich and KoelnRheinRuhr on Sep 26 (MDR, Aug 18). SZ reports federations expect a Munich v Rhine-Ruhr duel, and Rhine-Ruhr's 14M tickets score well in the DOSB matrix. Berlin has no referendum and Wegner has resigned.

Norris won Hungary and then the Dutch GP (Aug 23), so McLaren is back in contention. Antonelli was 2nd and leads Russell and Hamilton by 59 points; Verstappen crashed out. Mercedes' straight-line speed still suits Baku.

Ireland's settlement-goods ban was signed into law on Jul 23, Ireland holds the EU presidency and a services bill follows in September. That makes Ireland the likeliest target for Israeli retaliation. Slovenia was dropped because its new Jansa government plans to reverse recognition (Jun 28).

Sindhu lost a close Worlds R16 to Wang Zhiyi (Aug) after winning the Japan Open in July. Badminton runs Sep 20-29, so the Sep 27 resolution date lines up with quarterfinal day (resolved questions have resolution dates equal to the exit date).

NST (Aug 6): Sivasangari is world No. 5 and won the Australian Open and Grasshopper Cup this year, while Watanabe is No. 6 and plays at home. Anahat Singh (No. 20) won the World Junior title on Jul 25. Malaysia's second singles entrant is Aifa Azman.

Defending champion Ng Eain Yow (No. 18) has struggled on the PSA tour this year (NST Aug 6). His named rivals are Abhay Singh (No. 24), Noor Zaman (No. 29), Veer Chotrani (No. 38), Velavan Senthilkumar and Al-Tamimi.

The Sep 27 match in Debrecen is open to spectators with a small Israeli allocation, and the FAI will not seek tickets for Irish fans (Aug 4/14). Ireland remain slight favourites with little venue edge for either side.

Florida sued OpenAI on Jun 1; OpenAI removed it to federal court (Judge Cannon) and Florida is seeking remand. On Aug 4 a 15-state Republican AG coalition (incl. FL, TX, UT, MO) demanded OpenAI stop the testing behind the rogue-agent breach. NY and CO lead a separate multistate probe.

Pathirage beat Neeraj at Lausanne on Aug 21 (88.14 v 88.05), his third win over him in 2026 after Rome and CWG gold. Arshad finished outside the top 3 there. Rohit Yadav (87.05 SB) is on India's team.

Krack (Aug 20) says Aston Martin is 'fairly confident' of renewing Alonso, and The Race (Aug 21) says the direction of travel points to an extension. Alonso is still deciding and may take another role. Sainz (Williams, Aug 19) and Verstappen (Red Bull to 2030) are off the market.

Medias24 (Jul 23) says Istiqlal is no longer the clear favourite: PAM has momentum after recruiting Lekjaa, and RNI (led by Chaouki since Feb 7, Akhannouch still central) has the strongest machine. ExpressTV (Aug 11) frames it as an RNI v PAM duel; the vote is Sep 23.

China (2026 U23 Asian Cup runners-up) drew Group B with North Korea (Sep 16), Iran (Sep 20) and UAE (Sep 23). The QF is Sep 26 and the SF Sep 30 in Osaka, so the Sep 30 resolution date points to a semi-final exit.
